description:
The Organic Manure Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to promote sustainable agriculture practices. 

This scheme was officially launched in 2015 as part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture. 

The primary objective of the Organic Manure Scheme is to encourage farmers to adopt organic farming methods. 

The scheme aims to reduce the dependency on chemical fertilizers which can have detrimental effects on soil health and the environment. 

By promoting organic manure, the government seeks to enhance soil fertility and improve crop yields sustainably. 

The scheme also aims to increase the income of farmers by providing them with an alternative source of income through the production and sale of organic manure. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to increase the area under organic farming to 5 million hectares by 2025. 

The government has set a goal to train at least 1 million farmers in organic farming techniques by the end of 2025. 

Under the Organic Manure Scheme, various types of organic fertilizers are promoted. 

These include compost, vermicompost, biofertilizers, and other organic amendments. 

The benefits of the scheme are multifaceted. 

Farmers can receive financial assistance for setting up organic manure production units. 

The assistance can go up to 50 percent of the total project cost. 

For small and marginal farmers, the maximum limit of financial assistance is ₹1 lakh. 

For larger farmers, the limit is ₹2 lakh. 

The scheme also provides for the establishment of community composting units. 

These units can be set up with a maximum financial assistance of ₹5 lakh. 

The Organic Manure Scheme is designed to be inclusive. 

It targets small and marginal farmers who constitute about 86 percent of the total farming community in India. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a registered farmer. 

Farmers must also demonstrate a willingness to adopt organic farming practices. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, farmers must have access to land for cultivation. 

Income criteria are not strictly defined but preference is given to economically weaker sections. 

Educational qualifications are not a prerequisite for applying to the scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Farmers must first approach the nearest Agricultural Department office. 

They need to fill out the application form provided by the department. 

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, landholding details, and proposed project plan. 

Farmers must also submit documents such as land ownership proof and identity proof. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the Agricultural Officer. 

The officer may conduct a field visit to assess the feasibility of the proposed project. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed in installments. 

The first installment is released after the project is sanctioned. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The timeline for the application process can vary. 

Typically, it takes about 30 to 45 days for the application to be processed. 

Disbursement of funds usually occurs within 15 days after approval. 

The implementing authority for the Organic Manure Scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The scheme is executed through the State Agricultural Departments. 

Farmers can contact their local Agricultural Department for more information. 

The scheme also encourages the use of indigenous resources for organic manure production. 

This includes using farm waste, animal dung, and other biodegradable materials. 

The government provides training programs to educate farmers on organic manure production techniques. 

These training programs are conducted at various agricultural universities and institutions across the country. 

The Organic Manure Scheme is part of a larger initiative to promote organic farming in India. 

The government has also launched the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana to support organic farming. 

This scheme focuses on promoting organic farming through clusters and farmer producer organizations. 

The Organic Manure Scheme complements these efforts by providing the necessary inputs for organic farming. 

According to the Ministry of Agriculture, the organic farming sector in India has been growing at a rate of 25 percent annually. 

As of 2021, India had over 2.8 million hectares of land under organic cultivation. 

The government aims to increase this figure significantly through initiatives like the Organic Manure Scheme. 

Farmers adopting organic practices can benefit from premium prices for their produce. 

Organic products often fetch prices that are 20 to 30 percent higher than conventional products. 

The scheme also promotes the use of organic manure in various crops such as vegetables, fruits, and cereals. 

This diversification helps in improving the overall productivity of the agricultural sector. 

The Organic Manure Scheme is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

It contributes to goals related to zero hunger, sustainable agriculture, and responsible consumption. 

The scheme also plays a crucial role in enhancing biodiversity and ecosystem health. 

By reducing chemical inputs, the scheme helps in preserving the environment. 

Farmers participating in the scheme are encouraged to adopt integrated farming systems. 

These systems combine crop cultivation with livestock rearing and agroforestry. 

The Organic Manure Scheme is a vital step towards achieving food security in India. 

It empowers farmers to produce healthy food while maintaining ecological balance. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme's impact on agricultural practices. 

Regular assessments ensure that the objectives of the scheme are being met effectively. 

In conclusion, the Organic Manure Scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at promoting organic farming. 

It provides financial assistance and training to farmers while encouraging sustainable agricultural practices. 

The scheme is a significant move towards enhancing the livelihoods of farmers and ensuring food security in India.
